Relaas gegeven te requisitie van den heer landdrost Pieter Lourensz door den slaaf Pieter van Mallebaar, lijfeijgen van den oud burgerraad Sr. Andries Grové, sijnde van den volgende inhoud namentlijk:
html: Relaas gegeven te requisitie van den heer landdrost Pieter Lourensz door den slaaf Pieter van Mallebaar, lijfeijgen van den oud burgerraad Sr. Andries Grové, sijnde van den volgende inhoud namentlijk:

text: Dat hij relatant tusschen den 13 en 14 deeser, des ’snagts, op de plaats van zijn meesters schoonzoon, den oud heemraad Andries Brink geleegen in ’t district van Draakensteijn en gent. ’t Vischwaater, in het slaavenhuijs aldaar op de kooij leggende te slaapen, door het sterk geblaf der honden, wakker is geworden, begeevende sig naar buijten om te sien, wat er te doen was, ontwaarende hij relatant alsdoen, doordien het helder maaneschijn was, dat er eene van de camervensters van het huijs open stond, begeevende hem relatant weederom in het slaavenhuijs bij den slaaf Dramma, toebehoorende voorm. Brink, aan dewelke hij relatant bekend maakte, dat er een venster van de camer open stond; dat sulx mogelijk door drossers konde gedaan zijn; en dat hij sulx aan de knegt in de wandeling Schipper Jan gent., die ter dier tijd op zijn schoonmoeders plaats omtrent een uur daarvandaan geleegen, was, moeste gaan bekend maaken, dewelke ook aanstonds sig te paard naar derwaarts heeft begeeven; begeevende hij relatant sig alsdoen naar het woonhuijs, met een Hottentot gent. Piet, die aldaar meede woonagtig is, om te sien, wat er te doen was; en ook om vuur te maaken.
html: Dat hij relatant tusschen den 13 en 14 deeser, des ’snagts, op de plaats van zijn meesters schoonzoon, den oud heemraad Andries Brink geleegen in ’t district van Draakensteijn en gent. ’t Vischwaater, in het slaavenhuijs aldaar op de kooij leggende te slaapen, door het sterk geblaf der honden, wakker is geworden, begeevende sig naar buijten om te sien, wat er te doen was, ontwaarende hij relatant alsdoen, doordien het helder maaneschijn was, dat er eene van de camervensters van het huijs open stond, begeevende hem relatant weederom in het slaavenhuijs bij den slaaf Dramma, toebehoorende voorm. Brink, aan dewelke hij relatant bekend maakte, dat er een venster van de camer open stond; dat sulx mogelijk door drossers konde gedaan zijn; en dat hij sulx aan de knegt in de wandeling Schipper Jan gent., die ter dier tijd op zijn schoonmoeders plaats omtrent een uur daarvandaan geleegen, was, moeste gaan bekend maaken, dewelke ook aanstonds sig te paard naar derwaarts heeft begeeven; begeevende hij relatant sig alsdoen naar het woonhuijs, met een Hottentot gent. Piet, die aldaar meede woonagtig is, om te sien, wat er te doen was; en ook om vuur te maaken.

text: Dat hij relatant met gesz. Hottentot Piet, de klink van de combuijsdeur open gemaakt hebbende, en daarbinnen treedende, aanstonds ontwaart hebben, dat de meijd van gem. Brink Francina gent., die altijd ’s nagts in huijs bleef, in de combuijs dichte bij de handmoolen doot lag, waarop hij relatant vuur gemaakt hebbende, een kleijn eijndje kaars heeft aangestooken, en met den Hottentot Piet, de meijd Francina voorm. verders hebben besichtigt, siende zijl. alsdoen dat het bloed van die meijd langs de grond liep, en dat de voordeur van het huijs open stond, begeevende hun daarop weeder naar het slavenhuijs.
html: Dat hij relatant met gesz. Hottentot Piet, de klink van de combuijsdeur open gemaakt hebbende, en daarbinnen treedende, aanstonds ontwaart hebben, dat de meijd van gem. Brink Francina gent., die altijd ’s nagts in huijs bleef, in de combuijs dichte bij de handmoolen doot lag, waarop hij relatant vuur gemaakt hebbende, een kleijn eijndje kaars heeft aangestooken, en met den Hottentot Piet, de meijd Francina voorm. verders hebben besichtigt, siende zijl. alsdoen dat het bloed van die meijd langs de grond liep, en dat de voordeur van het huijs open stond, begeevende hun daarop weeder naar het slavenhuijs.

text: Dat des anderen daags ’s morgens de knegt t’ huijs komende, aldaar op de plaats vermiste, den slaaf Cupido van zijn relatants meester, en een Hottentot die aldaar meede woonagtig was Louis gent.
html: Dat des anderen daags ’s morgens de knegt t’ huijs komende, aldaar op de plaats vermiste, den slaaf Cupido van zijn relatants meester, en een Hottentot die aldaar meede woonagtig was Louis gent.

text: Dat een dag of twee na dato, hij relatant de beesten en paarden in ’t veld weijdende, bij hem gekomen is, voorm. Hottentot Louis, dewelken hij relatant afvroeg: waar de jonge Cupido was, daar denselven op antwoorden: Die leijt in ’t rivier, en heeft zijn [sic] selven dootgestooken, gaande hij relatant met gesz. Hottentot, naar het volk, dat op ’t land beesig was, om te ploegen, aan dewelke hij den Hottentot Louis voorm. overgegeeven hebbende, weederom naar zijn beesten en paarden terugge is gekeert.

Hottentot Louis, dewelken hij relatant afvroeg: waar de jonge Cupido was, daar denselven op antwoorden: Die leijt in ’t rivier, en heeft zijn [sic] selven dootgestooken, gaande hij relatant met gesz. Hottentot, naar het volk, dat op ’t land beesig was, om te ploegen, aan dewelke hij den Hottentot Louis voorm. overgegeeven hebbende, weederom naar zijn beesten en paarden terugge is gekeert.

text: Laatstelijk betuijgt den relatant nog, dat den Hottentot Louis, niet wel bij zijn sinnen is, gaande veeltijds alleenig al praatende en lachende, sonder ijmand bij zig te hebben.
html: Laatstelijk betuijgt den relatant nog, dat den Hottentot Louis, niet wel bij zijn sinnen is, gaande veeltijds alleenig al praatende en lachende, sonder ijmand bij zig te hebben.

text: Niets meer relateerende geeft den relatant voor reedenen van weetenschap als in den text, bereijd sijnde, als ’t mogte gerequireert werden, het voorenstaande ten allen tijden nader te sullen gestand doen.

text: Aldus gerelateerd aan Stellenbosch op den 24 September 1745 ten overstaan van den boode Jan van Ellewe ende de burger Pieter Wion als getuijgen hiertoe versogt.

text: Dit merk X heeft Pieter van Mallebaar selfs gestelt.

text: TRANSLATION

Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost Pieter Lourensz by the slave Pieter van Malabar, bondsman of the former burgher councillor, Sieur Andries Grové, being of the following content, namely:
html: Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost Pieter Lourensz by the slave Pieter van Malabar, bondsman of the former burgher councillor, Sieur Andries Grové, being of the following content, namely:

text: That on the night between the 13th and 14th of this month, when the deponent was lying asleep on his bed in the slave house on the farm of his master’s son-in-law, the former heemraad Andries Brink, situated in the district of Drakenstein and called Vischwater, he was roused by the heavy barking of the dogs. He then went outside to see what was going on, which is when the deponent noticed in the bright moonlight that one of the bedroom windows of the house was open. The deponent then again went into the slave house and to the slave Dramma, who belongs to aforementioned Brink, to whom he made known that one of the bedroom windows was open and that this was perhaps done by deserters, and that he should go and report this to the knecht, commonly known as Schipper Jan, who was at this time on his mother-in-law’s farm, situated about an hour from there. Which he then also immediately did, setting out to that place by horse, while the deponent went to the house with a Hottentot named Piet, who also lived there, to see what was to be done and also to make a fire.
html: That on the night between the 13th and 14th of this month, when the deponent was lying asleep on his bed in the slave house on the farm of his master’s son-in-law, the former heemraad Andries Brink, situated in the district of Drakenstein and called Vischwater, he was roused by the heavy barking of the dogs. He then went outside to see what was going on, which is when the deponent noticed in the bright moonlight that one of the bedroom windows of the house was open. The deponent then again went into the slave house and to the slave Dramma, who belongs to aforementioned Brink, to whom he made known that one of the bedroom windows was open and that this was perhaps done by deserters, and that he should go and report this to the knecht, commonly known as Schipper Jan, who was at this time on his mother-in-law’s farm, situated about an hour from there. Which he then also immediately did, setting out to that place by horse, while the deponent went to the house with a Hottentot named Piet, who also lived there, to see what was to be done and also to make a fire.

text: That when the deponent and the Hottentot Piet opened the latch of the kitchen door and stepped inside, they instantly noticed that the meijd of said Brink, named Francina, who always remained in the house at night, was lying dead in the kitchen, close to the handmill. Whereupon the deponent, after making a fire, lit a small bit of a candle and further examined with the Hottentot Piet the aforementioned meijd Francina, which is when they saw that the blood of this meijd was running on the ground and that the front door of the house was open, whereupon they again went to the slave house.
html: That when the deponent and the Hottentot Piet opened the latch of the kitchen door and stepped inside, they instantly noticed that the meijd of said Brink, named Francina, who always remained in the house at night, was lying dead in the kitchen, close to the handmill. Whereupon the deponent, after making a fire, lit a small bit of a candle and further examined with the Hottentot Piet the aforementioned meijd Francina, which is when they saw that the blood of this meijd was running on the ground and that the front door of the house was open, whereupon they again went to the slave house.

text: That in the morning of the following day, the knecht came home and found Cupido, a slave of his master, and a Hottentot named Louis, who also lived there, missing from the farm.
html: That in the morning of the following day, the knecht came home and found Cupido, a slave of his master, and a Hottentot named Louis, who also lived there, missing from the farm.

text: That a day or two after this, when the deponent was grazing the cattle and horses in the veld, there came to him the aforementioned Hottentot Louis, to whom he asked where the jongen Cupido was, to which the same answered: “He is lying by the river and has stabbed himself to death”. The deponent went with the said Hottentot to the volk who were busy ploughing the fields and to whom he handed over the aforementioned Hottentot Louis, and again returned to his cattle and horses.
html: That a day or two after this, when the deponent was grazing the cattle and horses in the veld, there came to him the aforementioned Hottentot Louis, to whom he asked where the jongen Cupido was, to which the same answered: “He is lying by the river and has stabbed himself to death”. The deponent went with the said Hottentot to the volk who were busy ploughing the fields and to whom he handed over the aforementioned Hottentot Louis, and again returned to his cattle and horses.

text: Finally the deponent also declares that the Hottentot Louis is not in his right mind, often talking and laughing all by himself, without having anybody with him.
html: Finally the deponent also declares that the Hottentot Louis is not in his right mind, often talking and laughing all by himself, without having anybody with him.

text: There being nothing more to relate, the deponent asserts to be convinced of the accuracy of his statement as in the text, being willing, if it may be required, to subsequently confirm the above at any time.
html: There being nothing more to relate, the deponent asserts to be convinced of the accuracy of his statement as in the text, being willing, if it may be required, to subsequently confirm the above at any time.

text: Thus related at Stellenbosch on 24 September 1745 in the presence of the messenger of the court, Jan van Ellewe, and the burgher Pieter Wion, requested as witnesses hereto.
html: Thus related at Stellenbosch on 24 September 1745 in the presence of the messenger of the court, Jan van Ellewe, and the burgher Pieter Wion, requested as witnesses hereto.

text: This mark X was set down by Pieter van Malabar himself.

text: As witnesses, [signed] J. van Ellewe, Pieter Wion.

text: With my cognisance, [signed] A. Schephausen, secretary.

Relaas gegeeven ter requisitie van den heer landdrost Pieter Lourensz, door den Hottentot Piet, zijnde woonagtig op de plaats van den oud heemraad Andries Brink, weesende van den volgenden inhoud, namentlijk:
html: Relaas gegeeven ter requisitie van den heer landdrost Pieter Lourensz, door den Hottentot Piet, zijnde woonagtig op de plaats van den oud heemraad Andries Brink, weesende van den volgenden inhoud, namentlijk:

text: Dat hij relatant tusschen den 13 en 14 deeser des ’snagts, op de bovengen. plaats gent. ’t Vischwaater, in ’t slaavenhuijs aldaar op de kooij leggende, om te slaapen, uijt het woonhuijs op de plaats, binnen is gekomen, den slaaf Cupido toebehoorende den oud burgerraad Sr. Andries Grové, denwelken hem relatant en zijn broeder den Hottentot Louis gent., vroeg, om meede te gaan naar de plaats van den burger Pieter van Taak, om dacha te soeken, waarop zij beijde opstaande, zijn gemte. broeder Louis met de slaaf Cupido is gegaan, gaande hij relatant, vermits sig bedacht hadde, weederom op den kooij leggen.
html: Dat hij relatant tusschen den 13 en 14 deeser des ’snagts, op de bovengen. plaats gent. ’t Vischwaater, in ’t slaavenhuijs aldaar op de kooij leggende, om te slaapen, uijt het woonhuijs op de plaats, binnen is gekomen, den slaaf Cupido toebehoorende den oud burgerraad Sr. Andries Grové, denwelken hem relatant en zijn broeder den Hottentot Louis gent., vroeg, om meede te gaan naar de plaats van den burger Pieter van Taak, om dacha te soeken, waarop zij beijde opstaande, zijn gemte. broeder Louis met de slaaf Cupido is gegaan, gaande hij relatant, vermits sig bedacht hadde, weederom op den kooij leggen.

text: Dat omtrent ’s middernagts de honden sterk blaffende, de slaaf Pieter toebehoorende voorm. Sr. Grové, die aldaar ter dier tijd sig meede bevond, naar buijten is gegaan, komende kort daaraan weeder naar binnen, seggende teegens hem relatant en de slaaf Dramma van voornden. Brink, dat een camervenster open stond, en dat gem. Dramma oversulx aanstonds de knegt in de wandeling gent. Schipper Jan, die ter selver tijds op zijn moeders plaats omtrent een uur van daar geleegen, was, daarvan moeste gaan bericht geeven; dewelke dan ook aanstonds te paard ten dien eijnde derwaarts is gereeden.
html: Dat omtrent ’s middernagts de honden sterk blaffende, de slaaf Pieter toebehoorende voorm. Sr. Grové, die aldaar ter dier tijd sig meede bevond, naar buijten is gegaan, komende kort daaraan weeder naar binnen, seggende teegens hem relatant en de slaaf Dramma van voornden. Brink, dat een camervenster open stond, en dat gem. Dramma oversulx aanstonds de knegt in de wandeling gent. Schipper Jan, die ter selver tijds op zijn moeders plaats omtrent een uur van daar geleegen, was, daarvan moeste gaan bericht geeven; dewelke dan ook aanstonds te paard ten dien eijnde derwaarts is gereeden.

text: Dat na gemte. slaaf Dramma was weggereeden, den slaaf Pieter voormt. teegens hem relatant heeft gesegd: Kom, laaten wij naar huijs gaan, om te sien, wat er te doen is, jij moet niet bang weesen; waarop hij relatant sig met den slaaf Pieter naar het woonhuijs heeft begeeven, gaande naar de klink van de combuijsdeur open gedaan hadden, in die combuijs, vindende soo dra binnen waren gekomen, de slavinne Francina, van voormten. Andries Brink, op de grond dichte bij de handmoolen, doot leggen, waarop zij vuur gemaakt en een kaars opgestooken hebbende, ontwaart hebben, dat voorsz. meijd op de rechter zijde doot lag, en dat er een heele plas bloed rondom haar was, en siende dat de voordeur van het huijs open was; welke door haar toegedaan weesende, is hij relatant met den slaaf Pieter weeder naar het slavenhuijs terugge gekeert.
html: Dat na gemte. slaaf Dramma was weggereeden, den slaaf Pieter voormt. teegens hem relatant heeft gesegd: Kom, laaten wij naar huijs gaan, om te sien, wat er te doen is, jij moet niet bang weesen; waarop hij relatant sig met den slaaf Pieter naar het woonhuijs heeft begeeven, gaande naar de klink van de combuijsdeur open gedaan hadden, in die combuijs, vindende soo dra binnen waren gekomen, de slavinne Francina, van voormten. Andries Brink, op de grond dichte bij de handmoolen, doot leggen, waarop zij vuur gemaakt en een kaars opgestooken hebbende, ontwaart hebben, dat voorsz. meijd op de rechter zijde doot lag, en dat er een heele plas bloed rondom haar was, en siende dat de voordeur van het huijs open was; welke door haar toegedaan weesende, is hij relatant met den slaaf Pieter weeder naar het slavenhuijs terugge gekeert.

text: Dat omtrent teegens den dag, den slaaf Pieter, hem relatant heeft gelast, een paard te neemen, om de knegt kennisse te geeven, dat de meijd doot was, waarop hij relatant een paard uijt de stal genomen hebbende, en sig op weg begeevende, niet verre van de plaats, den voorm. slaaf Dramma is ontmoet, aan denwelke hij relatant seijde dat de meijd Francina doot was; en dat sulx aan de knegt moeste bekend maaken, dewelke daarop antwoorde, dat de knegt aanstonds komen souden, keerende hij relatant daarop met voorm. Dramma weederom terugge naar huijs, rijdende eeven gemten. Dramma, kort daaraan weederom te paard naar de knegt om hem van alles kennisse te geeven, als meede dat den slaaf Cupido van voorm. Sr. Grove, die aldaar meede op de post bescheijden was, en zijn relatants broeder Louis, die sig daar verhuurt hadde, op de plaats niet present waren.
html: Dat omtrent teegens den dag, den slaaf Pieter, hem relatant heeft gelast, een paard te neemen, om de knegt kennisse te geeven, dat de meijd doot was, waarop hij relatant een paard uijt de stal genomen hebbende, en sig op weg begeevende, niet verre van de plaats, den voorm. slaaf Dramma is ontmoet, aan denwelke hij relatant seijde dat de meijd Francina doot was; en dat sulx aan de knegt moeste bekend maaken, dewelke daarop antwoorde, dat de knegt aanstonds komen souden, keerende hij relatant daarop met voorm. Dramma weederom terugge naar huijs, rijdende eeven gemten. Dramma, kort daaraan weederom te paard naar de knegt om hem van alles kennisse te geeven, als meede dat den slaaf Cupido van voorm. Sr. Grove, die aldaar meede op de post bescheijden was, en zijn relatants broeder Louis, die sig daar verhuurt hadde, op de plaats niet present waren.

text: Dat des ’s morgens omtrent acht uuren de knegt t’ huijs komende, hem relatant heeft geroepen en gelast, dat met de schaapen in ’t veld soude gaan, ’twelke hij relat. ook gedaan heeft.
html: Dat des ’s morgens omtrent acht uuren de knegt t’ huijs komende, hem relatant heeft geroepen en gelast, dat met de schaapen in ’t veld soude gaan, ’twelke hij relat. ook gedaan heeft.

text: Dat omtrent twee daagen na dato den slaaf Pieter voornt., met zijn relatants broeder voornt. Louis gent. bij haarl. op het land bij de ploeg gekomen is, als wanneer hij relatant naar huijs is gegaan, en de knegt sulx heeft bekend gemaakt, welkes [sic] huijsvrouw met hem relatant meede gegaan is, naar de ploeg, belastende bij haar aankomst, den Hottentot Louis vast te binden en naar huijs te brengen, ’twelk door hem relatant en de andere slaven ook is verrigt geworden, seggende gem. knegt teegens den Hottentot Louis, dat de plaats soude aanwijsen, waar de slaaf Cupido sig doot gestooken hadde; gaande de knegt, hij relatant en de andere slaven, met de Hottentot Louis dewelke dan ook omtrent een half uur gaans daar van daan de goederen als de slaaf Cupido heeft aangeweesen, leggende dien slaaf voorover op zijn buijk te sieltoogen, belastende de knegt hem relatant, om te gaan naar de plaats van den burger Pieter van Taak, om denselven te versoeken, bij hem te komen, vanwaar hij relatant weeder terug bij de knegt komende, sag dat den slaaf Cupido bereeds den geest gegeeven hadde.

text: Laatstelijk betuijgt den relatant nog, dat den Hottentot Louis, niet wel bij zijn sinnen is, gaande veeltijds alleenig, praatende, lachende en dansende, sonder dat ijmand bij hem is.

text: TRANSLATION
Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost Pieter Lourensz by the Hottentot Piet, living on the farm of the former heemraad Andries Brink, being of the following content, namely:
html: Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost Pieter Lourensz by the Hottentot Piet, living on the farm of the former heemraad Andries Brink, being of the following content, namely:

text: That during the night of the 13th and 14th of this month the deponent was lying asleep on the bed in the slave house on the abovementioned farm, called Vischwater, when the slave Cupido, who belongs to the former burgher councillor, Sieur Andries Grové, came inside from the house on the farm and asked the deponent and his brother, the Hottentot named Louis, to go with him to the farm of the burgher Pieter van Taak in order to search for dagga, whereupon they both got up and his aforementioned brother Louis went with the slave Cupido, while the deponent, since he thought better of it, again went to lie on his bed.
html: That during the night of the 13th and 14th of this month the deponent was lying asleep on the bed in the slave house on the abovementioned farm, called Vischwater, when the slave Cupido, who belongs to the former burgher councillor, Sieur Andries Grové, came inside from the house on the farm and asked the deponent and his brother, the Hottentot named Louis, to go with him to the farm of the burgher Pieter van Taak in order to search for dagga, whereupon they both got up and his aforementioned brother Louis went with the slave Cupido, while the deponent, since he thought better of it, again went to lie on his bed.

text: That at about midnight, when the dogs were barking heavily, the slave Pieter, who belongs to the aforementioned Sieur Grové, who at this time was also there [on the farm], went outside, returning again shortly thereafter, saying to the deponent and the slave Dramma of aforementioned Brink, that a bedroom window was open and that the said Dramma therefore had to go and inform the knecht, commonly known as Schipper Jan, who was at this time on his mother’s farm situated about an hour from there, about this; who then also to this end forthwith rode there by horse.
html: That at about midnight, when the dogs were barking heavily, the slave Pieter, who belongs to the aforementioned Sieur Grové, who at this time was also there [on the farm], went outside, returning again shortly thereafter, saying to the deponent and the slave Dramma of aforementioned Brink, that a bedroom window was open and that the said Dramma therefore had to go and inform the knecht, commonly known as Schipper Jan, who was at this time on his mother’s farm situated about an hour from there, about this; who then also to this end forthwith rode there by horse.

text: That after the said Dramma had ridden off, the aforementioned slave Pieter said to the deponent: “Come, let us go to the house to see what is to be done, you must not be afraid”, whereupon he went with the slave Pieter to the house; entering, after opening the latch of the door, the kitchen, where they found upon entering the woman slave Francina of aforementioned Andries Brink lying dead on the ground close to the hand mill. Upon this, they made a fire, lit a candle, and discovered that the aforesaid meijd was lying dead on her right hand side and that there was a whole pool of blood around her, and also saw that the front door of the house was open, which door was closed by them. The deponent, then returned again with the slave Pieter to the slave house.
html: That after the said Dramma had ridden off, the aforementioned slave Pieter said to the deponent: “Come, let us go to the house to see what is to be done, you must not be afraid”, whereupon he went with the slave Pieter to the house; entering, after opening the latch of the door, the kitchen, where they found upon entering the woman slave Francina of aforementioned Andries Brink lying dead on the ground close to the hand mill. Upon this, they made a fire, lit a candle, and discovered that the aforesaid meijd was lying dead on her right hand side and that there was a whole pool of blood around her, and also saw that the front door of the house was open, which door was closed by them. The deponent, then returned again with the slave Pieter to the slave house.

text: That at about day break the slave Pieter ordered him to take a horse to inform the knecht that the meijd was dead, whereupon the deponent took a horse from the stable and set out on the road. Not far from the farm he met the aforementioned slave Dramma – whom he told that the meijd Francina was dead and that he, the deponent, should go to inform the knecht about this – who answered that the knecht would be arriving presently. Upon that the deponent returned home again with the aforementioned Dramma, while Dramma shortly thereupon again rode by horse to the knecht to inform him of everything, and that the slave Cupido of the aforementioned Sieur Grové, who was also assigned to the post, and his brother Louis, who had rented himself out there, were not present on the farm.
html: That at about day break the slave Pieter ordered him to take a horse to inform the knecht that the meijd was dead, whereupon the deponent took a horse from the stable and set out on the road. Not far from the farm he met the aforementioned slave Dramma – whom he told that the meijd Francina was dead and that he, the deponent, should go to inform the knecht about this – who answered that the knecht would be arriving presently. Upon that the deponent returned home again with the aforementioned Dramma, while Dramma shortly thereupon again rode by horse to the knecht to inform him of everything, and that the slave Cupido of the aforementioned Sieur Grové, who was also assigned to the post, and his brother Louis, who had rented himself out there, were not present on the farm.

text: That at about 8 o’clock that morning the knecht came home, called the deponent and ordered him to go with the sheep into the veld, which is what the deponent did.
html: That at about 8 o’clock that morning the knecht came home, called the deponent and ordered him to go with the sheep into the veld, which is what the deponent did.

text: That about two days after this, the aforementioned slave Pieter came to them in the fields at the plough with his brother, the aforementioned Louis, which is when the deponent went to the house and informed the knecht of this, whose wife went with the deponent to the plough and on her arrival ordered them to tie up the Hottentot Louis and to take him to the house, which was also done by the deponent and the other slaves. The said knecht then told the Hottentot Louis that he must point out the place where the slave Cupido had stabbed himself to death. Hereafter the knecht, the deponent and the other slaves went with the Hottentot Louis who, about half an hour from there, indicated an object as the slave Cupido, who was lying prostrate on his stomach in the pangs of death. The knecht ordered the deponent to go to the farm of the burgher Pieter van Taak to request the same to come to him. When the deponent again returned from there to the knecht, he saw that the slave Cupido had already given up the ghost.

The said knecht then told the Hottentot Louis that he must point out the place where the slave Cupido had stabbed himself to death. Hereafter the knecht, the deponent and the other slaves went with the Hottentot Louis who, about half an hour from there, indicated an object as the slave Cupido, who was lying prostrate on his stomach in the pangs of death. The knecht ordered the deponent to go to the farm of the burgher Pieter van Taak to request the same to come to him. When the deponent again returned from there to the knecht, he saw that the slave Cupido had already given up the ghost.

text: Finally, the deponent also declares that the Hottentot Louis is not in his right mind, often going talking, laughing and dancing all by himself, without anybody being with him.
html: Finally, the deponent also declares that the Hottentot Louis is not in his right mind, often going talking, laughing and dancing all by himself, without anybody being with him.

text: There being nothing further to relate, the deponent asserts to be convinced of the accuracy of his statement as in the text, while offering, if it may be required, to subsequently confirm this, his statement, at any time.

text: Dat nu omtrent 3 ß 4 weeken geleeden, zij relatante op haar moeder, de weduwe Francois Retiefs plaats geleegen aan Draakensteijn, op seekeren nagt leggende te slaapen, en haar relatantes moeder, eenig gewag in huijs hoorende, opgestaan weesende, en ontwaart hebbende, dat er een camervenster, hetwelke aan de andere kant van het huijs was, openstond, haar relatante heeft geroepen, waarop opstaande en bij haar moeder gekomen zijnde, met deselve in die camer is gegaan, siende zijl. alsdoen, dat er twee geweeren dewelke Æs avonds bevorens op het geweerrak geleegen hadden, bij het open gemaakte venster stonden, waarop zij relatante die twee geweeren weggenomen en het venster weederom toegemaakt hebbende, een weijnigje [sic] daaraan, met de kaars weederom in de camer is gegaan, ontdekkende alsdoen, dat er een gat in het dak gebrooken was.

text: Nog betuijgt de relatante, dat haare moeder eenige daagen bevorens, vier beesten heeft vermist, waarvan thans drie weederom bekomen hebben.

text: TRANSLATION
Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost, Pieter Lourensz, by the maiden Magdalena Retief, 24 years old, which is of the following content, namely:
html: Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost, Pieter Lourensz, by the maiden Magdalena Retief, 24 years old, which is of the following content, namely:

text: That on a certain night, about three to four weeks ago now, when the deponent was lying asleep at the farm, situated in Drakenstein, belonging to her mother, the widow of Francois Retief, her mother heard some commotion, got up and noticed that a bedroom window, which was on the other side of the house, was open; and called to the deponent, who then got up, went to her mother and entered this bedroom with her, which is when they saw that two guns, which the previous evening were on the gun-rack, were standing by the opened window. The deponent then took away these two guns and closed the window again, and a short while thereafter, when she again went into the room, she discovered that there was a hole broken into the roof.
html: That on a certain night, about three to four weeks ago now, when the deponent was lying asleep at the farm, situated in Drakenstein, belonging to her mother, the widow of Francois Retief, her mother heard some commotion, got up and noticed that a bedroom window, which was on the other side of the house, was open; and called to the deponent, who then got up, went to her mother and entered this bedroom with her, which is when they saw that two guns, which the previous evening were on the gun-rack, were standing by the opened window. The deponent then took away these two guns and closed the window again, and a short while thereafter, when she again went into the room, she discovered that there was a hole broken into the roof.

text: The deponent also declares that some days previously four cattle of her mother had gone missing, of which she had by now recovered three.
html: The deponent also declares that some days previously four cattle of her mother had gone missing, of which she had by now recovered three.

Relaas gegeeven ter requisitie van den heer landdrost Pieter Lourensz, door den burger Jacobus Marais, sijnde van den volgenden inhoud, namentlijk:
html: Relaas gegeeven ter requisitie van den heer landdrost Pieter Lourensz, door den burger Jacobus Marais, sijnde van den volgenden inhoud, namentlijk:

text: Dat hij relatant op Saturdag den 17e April jongstleeden, met zijn huijsvrouw, van desselfs woonplaats geleegen in de Waagenmaakersvalleij, naar zijn relatants schoonmoeder de weduwe Francois Retief rijdende, en des Maandags morgens weederom tÆ huijs komende, ontwaarde, dat er een camervenster opengebrooken was, sijnde de bovenste duijm van deselve uijt het cosijn gebrooken, siende voorts in huijs komende, dat de camerdeur van binnen geopent en daaruijt gestoolen was, vijf broeken, een waakrok, een manel [sic], twee brooden, eenig meel en twee hoeden, missende hij relatant tegelijk eenig vleesch, Ætwelk in een vleeschvat in het voorhuijs gestaan hadde, ontdekkende, hij relatant kort daaraan meede, dat een venster van de wijnkelder, æt welk door hem toegeklaaijt [sic] sijnde, ingsgelijx doorgebrooken was, en dat uijt deselve, een kan en eenig wijn gestoolen was.
html: Dat hij relatant op Saturdag den 17e April jongstleeden, met zijn huijsvrouw, van desselfs woonplaats geleegen in de Waagenmaakersvalleij, naar zijn relatants schoonmoeder de weduwe Francois Retief rijdende, en des Maandags morgens weederom tÆ huijs komende, ontwaarde, dat er een camervenster opengebrooken was, sijnde de bovenste duijm van deselve uijt het cosijn gebrooken, siende voorts in huijs komende, dat de camerdeur van binnen geopent en daaruijt gestoolen was, vijf broeken, een waakrok, een manel [sic], twee brooden, eenig meel en twee hoeden, missende hij relatant tegelijk eenig vleesch, Ætwelk in een vleeschvat in het voorhuijs gestaan hadde, ontdekkende, hij relatant kort daaraan meede, dat een venster van de wijnkelder, æt welk door hem toegeklaaijt [sic] sijnde, ingsgelijx doorgebrooken was, en dat uijt deselve, een kan en eenig wijn gestoolen was.

text: Dat hij relatant daarop eenige van zijne buuren versogt hebbende, met hem meede te gaan, omme die dieven op te soeken, met deselve naar het gebergte is gemarcheert, alwaar spoor van eenige schaapen en twee persoonen die barrevoets gegaan hadden, gevonden hebben, Ætwelk zijlieden tot op het gebergte hebben gevolgt, vindende des anderen daags agter dat gebergte, elf schaapen die meede uijt zijn relatants troup gestoolen waren.
html: Dat hij relatant daarop eenige van zijne buuren versogt hebbende, met hem meede te gaan, omme die dieven op te soeken, met deselve naar het gebergte is gemarcheert, alwaar spoor van eenige schaapen en twee persoonen die barrevoets gegaan hadden, gevonden hebben, Ætwelk zijlieden tot op het gebergte hebben gevolgt, vindende des anderen daags agter dat gebergte, elf schaapen die meede uijt zijn relatants troup gestoolen waren.

text: Dat hij relatant tÆ huijs komende, van zijne huijsvrouw verstaan heeft, dat eenige van zijne slaaven, het voormte. gestoolen goed, omtrent een quartier uur van zijn relatants wooning af, verstrooijt in de boschjes hadden vinden leggen, beneevens een snaphaan van Francois Retief, die door een slaaf van denselven gent. Januarij van Rio de la Goa, die ter dier tijd fugatief sijnde, meede genomen was; missende hij relatant alsdoen niet meer als twee broeken en de waakrok, dewelke hij relatant weederom bekomen heeft, wanneer de slaaf Arend toebehoorende den burger Hendrik Hoppe, gevangen genomen wierd, dewelke alsdoen een van de broeken aanhad, en de waakrok en andere broek aanwees.

Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost, Pieter Lourensz, by the burgher Jacobus Marais, which is of the following content, namely:
html: Statement given on the requisition of the honourable landdrost, Pieter Lourensz, by the burgher Jacobus Marais, which is of the following content, namely:

text: That on Saturday 17 April of this year, the deponent rode with his wife from his residential farm situated in the Wagenmakersvallei to his mother-in-law, the widow Francois Retief, and coming back home again on the Monday morning, noticed that a bedroom window was broken into and that the top inch of the same was broken out of the frame, seeing further when he went into the house that the bedroom door was opened from the inside and that five pairs of trousers, an oilskin coat, a frock, two loaves of bread, some flour and two hats were stolen from there; at the same time the deponent also found missing some meat which was in a meat tub standing in the front room. Shortly thereafter the deponent also discovered that a window of the wine cellar, which had been locked by him, was likewise broken into and that a tankard and some wine were stolen from it.

Shortly thereafter the deponent also discovered that a window of the wine cellar, which had been locked by him, was likewise broken into and that a tankard and some wine were stolen from it.

text: That thereupon the deponent requested some of his neighbours to go with him to search for these thieves, and went with the same to the mountain where they found traces of some sheep and two persons who were going barefoot, which they followed to the top of the mountain, finding the following day on the other side of that mountain eleven sheep which had also been stolen from his flock.

text: That when the deponent came home, he understood from his wife that some of his slaves had found, lying scattered around in the bushes about a quarter of an hour from his residence, the aforementioned stolen goods, as also a musket of Francois Retief, which had been stolen by a slave of the same called Januarij van Rio de la Goa, who was at this time a fugitive. The deponent then did not have anything missing except two pairs of trousers and the oilskin coat, which he recovered again when the slave Aaron, belonging to the burgher Hendrik Hoppe, was taken prisoner, who was at that time wearing one of these trousers and who pointed out the coat and other trousers.

text: That in the month of April this year, without knowing the exact date, when the deponent came home from the Cape to his farm, situated near the Groeneberg, he understood from his wife that during his absence two runaway slaves, of which the one belongs to the burgher Hendrik Hoppe and the other to the burgher Francois Retief, had broken a hole into his wheat house and went inside through it. heading: 1745 to 181[?] — Manomia, Clasina of Bengal
text: 1745 to 181[?] — Manomia, Clasina of Bengal
html: 1745 to 181[?] — Manomia, Clasina of Bengal

text: Manomia, Clasina of Bengal, 1745-181[?]
Editor’s introduction

One of the extraordinary aspects of this document is that although baptism, according to the  Synod of Dort (q.v.), was substantial grounds for claiming Christian freedom,  Clasina was the only slave who brought a legal case before the Cape courts claiming freedom solely on the basis of baptism.  The Cape prosecutors who won the case against her, warped (no other word will do) the preceding legislation and the only legal principle of Christian universalism. It was widely believed at the Cape that baptism did entail profound civic rights.  Yet Clasina was the only slave to bring a case for herself and her children on these grounds.  It is also ironic that Steijntje of the Cape who also brought a case claiming freedom, but did so on grounds of cohabiting with a person of European descent, should go free.  Racial descent, according to the Cape court, had become more important than religious status.

The Cape prosecutors who won the case against her, warped (no other word will do) the preceding legislation and the only legal principle of Christian universalism. It was widely believed at the Cape that baptism did entail profound civic rights. Yet Clasina was the only slave to bring a case for herself and her children on these grounds. It is also ironic that Steijntje of the Cape who also brought a case claiming freedom, but did so on grounds of cohabiting with a person of European descent, should go free. Racial descent, according to the Cape court, had become more important than religious status.

text: And whereas the Petitioner as a Christian for the clearing of her conscience before God as well as her children, in her decrepit age, and before her death could wish to know from whence the state of slavery of her children has its origin, the Petitioner addresses herself to Your Excellency, so as she takes the liberty to do by these Presents, with a very humble request that it may graciously please Your Excellency for her comfort to cause an enquiry to be made in the said matter so and in such a manner as Your Excellency in highest wisdom shall judge proper.

text: The undersigned advocate humbly represents that having received your Worships' commands, whereby he was appointed and nominated Trustee on behalf of one Clasina (requesting an investigation into the case of her children and grandchildren, who are kept in slavery, but whom she asserts to be free) to conduct her concerns and those of her children and grandchildren, has immediately undertaken an enquiry into the case of the said Clasina since her arrival in this Colony. The said Clasina informed him that her father and mother were slaves to Mr. Zigterman, that the said gentlemen and his wife touched here on their return to Europe, and then took her mother with them to Holland, leaving her (Clasina) here in slavery under the authority and in the service of the late Mr.  Blankenberg, promising that they would write to her from Holland and have her brought over, yet that this never took place, but that she was some years after placed under the direction of P. J. Truter, Esqre., who was then married to Miss Hannetje Blankenberg, and with whom she has hitherto remained; that she has no proof whatsoever of her freedom, but that she was instigated by her children and particularly by Marie, slave of the widow P.  de Waal, to sign the memorial to his Lordship.

Further the new Statutes of India, Title Slaves, Article 9, in conformity to the resolution of the Chief Government, dated 10th April 1770, run as follows:

text: “The Christians are bound to instruct their slaves in the Christian religion and have them baptized, if they be inclined or can be induced thereto, using the least forcible means, on pain of arbitrary correction, and those who have been confirmed in the Christian religion may not be sold, but their masters are obliged at their death or departure from this country to emancipate all such slaves, or present them or bequeath them to others under the same obligation, or at their departure from India to transfer them, at a reasonable valuation either by the messengers of the board of schepenen, or orphan masters, or the auctioneer of the town vendue master, to such persons as may be willing to take them over and manumit them, as also to allow all such slaves as are born in the family or are presents to purchase their freedom themselves at prime cost or at valuation.”

text: This law then gives no immediate freedom to the baptized slaves. Moreover this law is subsequent to the baptism of Clasina, and thus can have no retrospective effect, as Clasina was baptized in the year 1745, a period when the proclamation of the Governor General Van Diemen of the year 1642, with respect to the baptism of slaves, was only applicable, and in which was only to be found the following passage: “The Christians are bound to instruct their slaves in the Christian religion and have them baptized, on pain of arbitrary correction.” So that Clasina, in regard to her baptism alone, can have no claim to freedom.

text: The undersigned has however demanded of said P. J. Truter, Esquire, a proof of his property in Clasina, and received from him copy of a document hereunto annexed, from which it appears that the same Clasina was bequeathed by the late Johannes Henricus Blankenberg and Anna Margaretha van der Heyde, lawfully married persons, to their daughter Johanna Ernestina Blankenberg, who was afterwards married to P.J. Truter, Esquire, (and who bequeathed her to the same P. J. Truter, Esquire), as a slave by the name Manomia, surnamed Clasina of Bengal, and under this condition that neither she nor the children which she may hereafter bear shall ever be sold (except on account of very bad behaviour), but shall remain the property of said Johanna Ernestina and her heirs.

The word “person”
No. 5.
To J. H. Neethling, Esqre.

Sir,—In answer to your letter of the 26th instant I have the honor to state that the word Person (Persoon) was not used by me in the certificate of baptism of Clasina of Bengal to imply thereby the freedom of free birth of said Clasina, but merely in compliance with custom; for in the register of baptisms the same is used for all aged persons indiscriminately, whether they be manumitted, slaves, or free born. text: (Signed) J. H. von Manger.
Deposition by owner
No. 6.

We the undersigned Johannes Henricus Blankenberg and Anna Margaretha van der Heyde, lawfully married persons, declare and acknowledge to present, give, and transfer, as we do present, give, and transfer by these presents in full and free property unto our daughter Johanna Ernestina Blankenberg, one of our slave girls Manomia surnamed Clasina of Bengal, under condition that she and the children which she may hereafter bear shall not be sold, except on account of very bad behaviour, but shall remain the property of our said daughter Johanna Ernestina and her descendants, wherefore we renounce all right and property which we until this day had in the said female slave in favor as above, promising to free the property thus gifted and transferred from all encumbrances according to law.

From which papers (in the humble opinion of the undersigned) it appears

text: 1st. That Clasina could not bring forward anything to prove her freedom, only appealing to two letters which she according to the Revision ad idem on the 10th July still had in her possession, and which she received from her mother in Holland, but which according to No. 4 do not mention anything of her freedom, and further asserting to have been informed by her mother that she was free born, whereas she, according to No. 4, was only a child of 4 or 5 years when her mother left her here; it is improbable that a Governor returning to Europe would have no room on board for a child of 4 or 5 years, but should have preferred to deprive the parents of such a child and leave it here, and let the mother come over from Holland two years after expressly to take the child from hence rather than take it to Holland himself; it shows that the owner (whom she calls Mr.  Zigterman) must have given her to the late Mr. Blankenberg, and contained among others that her mother would come and fetch her two years after, but how is this to be believed, as the same Mr. Blankenberg has signed the deed of gift and conditional slavery on the 24th July 1771.

text: 2nd. It appears that Clasina bore no children after she was transferred to the deceased wife of P. J. Truter, Esquire, so that Mr. Truter never could have acted contrary to the conditions of the gift.

text: 3rd. It appears that prior to the said gift Clasina bore three children, named Theresia, Sanna, and Eleonora, of whom she says that Theresia is with Mrs. Brand and Susanna with Mrs. De Waal, and Eleonora was sold by the Orphan Chamber to Van der Heyde.

text: 4th. With regard to the daughter of Clasina named Eleonora, it appears that in the year 1773 the said Eleonora was entered on the inventory of the estate of the late Blankenberg by the Board of the Orphan Masters administering the said estate, as unconditional property, by the name of Eleonora of the Cape, whereas the conditions then mentioned in the inventory in regard to the slaves Carcat and Rosetta show that the slaves belonging to the estate were distinctly entered on the list with the conditions of slavery (if any were found), which was not the case with said Eleonora. It is evident that if at that time as well Clasina as the said Eleonora or her sister Susanna who still belonged to the estate (although presented to Christina Magdalena Blankenberg) had any idea of freedom, one of them would certainly have applied to the said Board in order to obtain their manumission, while on the contrary said Eleonora was sold by the Board of Orphan Masters at public sale, of whose freedom thus not the least proof exists or has existed.

Laubscher, all publicly and as slaves, so that certainly with regard to Eleonora and her descendants no trace of freedom will be found.

Brand, Esquire, on the very same conditions of which Clasina was gifted to the wife of Mr. Truter; while we learn that Theresia was sold by said Mr. Brand on account of her bad conduct, and that Claas Peters has a daughter of hers. And with respect to this daughter it appears that she is named Sylvia, found by him as slave in the estate of his first wife, and that a brother of Sylvia was either to be found at D. van Reenen's or on Robben Island, and No. 10, Art. 2, shows that the latter (being the slave of J. C. de Wet) was banished to Robben Island by sentence of the Worshipful Court, and said Sylvia says that the one brother belongs to D. G. van Reenen and the other to J. C. de Wet, the latter being on Robben Island.

Dreyer, Telemachus to Smitsdorff, Mary and Saartje are bought by their husbands.

text: And all this agrees with the declaration of these slaves, while the Widow de Waal called God Almighty to witness her declaration that she sold the slaves to Dreyer and Smitsdorff on account of their extreme bad behaviour (considering principally in drinking and gambling), that as long as her husband was alive she could keep them in order, but that after his death she was obliged to dispose of many of those slaves, and that the present examination has greatly increased her sorrow and trouble proceeding from the slaves still in her possession, so that two of them having obtained permission to hire themselves out did not bring in the amount hire for two months and were insolent to her besides, which declaration the purchaser Dreyer has confirmed with regard to those belonging to him, saying that the reasons why he bought those slaves were that they having been let to him formerly the one committed theft and the other behaved himself improperly, and that afterwards both ran away as well as their brother Telemachus who was sold to one Smitsdorff, that he being unwilling to hire them any longer sent them back to Mrs. De Waal, but that said Mrs. De Waal afterwards informed him that she could not agree with those slaves, when he became owner of them by purchase. And Smitsdorff also says with regard to his slave that the said slave Telemachus is obstinate and disobedient, and that he has therefore let him in order to get rid of him, while Anna de Waal states that she became owner of hers by purchase from her mother, which is in conformity to the deed of gift that the slave Susanna and her children shall remain the property of the person to whom they were given and his or her heir.

And Smitsdorff also says with regard to his slave that the said slave Telemachus is obstinate and disobedient, and that he has therefore let him in order to get rid of him, while Anna de Waal states that she became owner of hers by purchase from her mother, which is in conformity to the deed of gift that the slave Susanna and her children shall remain the property of the person to whom they were given and his or her heir.

text: After having thus, Worshipful Gentlemen, (as the undersigned respectfully trusts) in consequence of the Worshipful Court's intention traced the whole relation of Clasina over which he was appointed trustee, and as is mentioned before the undersigned is of opinion that the sale of Eleonora as free and unconditional property already proves, that neither her mother nor any of the children have reported themselves to the Board as free persons, but on the contrary have consented to the sale of their respective daughter or sister, which serves thus as a proof that they and Eleonora acknowledged themselves to be slaves; that Mr. P. Truter became owner of the said Clasina by gift, Mr. De Waal of a second daughter of hers in the same manner, and the late Van der Heyde of a third daughter of Clasina by public purchase; and that from the year 1773 to 1810 (thus by a possession and lapse of time of 37 years before there existed any question of freedom) that right is confirmed to the owners, that there also exist no traces of freedom, but that their silence during that time proves their conviction of being slaves; that also Mr. Brand and Mrs. De Waal according to their deeds of gift had a right to sell their slaves on account of bad conduct, and finally that if we justly consider it, it shows us that the possession is a true title of the possessors, that the accusation of possessing a person as slave who is free charges the original possessors with a fraudulent design and an act of capture whereby a certain person is deprived of his freedom, but which fraud may not be supposed, but must be proved; that all the proprietors, viz. P. J. Truter, Esqre., C. Brand, Esquire, Mrs. P. de Waal, and P. Schreuder, have proved their legal property, and thus the accusation of Clasina can only affect such acts as were committed by deceased persons who enjoyed a good reputation, and who have confirmed the legality of their acts at their death, as this legality is the more confirmed by a silence of 37 years of those interested, without any reasons having been stated by them or any apparent motive having been traced why they, or at least one of them, have not complained of their being illegally kept in slavery, or have taken any steps of the same nature as the present accusation hazarded to prove their having been deprived of freedom, which could never have been done more properly than at the time when the Orphan Chamber administered the estate of their donors as an impartial Board which had no interest in their freedom or slavery.

text: On these grounds then the undersigned requests to be released from the appointment of trustee over people of whose suppositions of freedom he declares to find no title, but on the contrary (on account of a possession and silence of 37 years added to the grounds before alluded to) voluntarily presumes to give his opinion as to the legality of their slavery, while on the other hand the undersigned Advocate (as he respectfully trusts) is sufficiently known to this Worshipful Court to be ready and willing in all cases (if convinced of the justice of the claim) without respect of persons to plead for the legal freedom of human beings who are illegally kept in slavery, and particularly when called upon by the judge to proceed against every illegal possessor requesting therefore your Worships' honored reply.

text: 1. Her name, age, and where born? Says: Clasina, my age I do not know, but I believe full 70 years, I was born in Bengal, was six years old when I came to the Cape.
html: 1. Her name, age, and where born? Says: Clasina, my age I do not know, but I believe full 70 years, I was born in Bengal, was six years old when I came to the Cape.

text: 2. How she and her parents became the slaves of Mr. Zigterman? My mother suckled Mr. Zigterman's child, and I was born in his house;  Mr. Zigterman brought me with my father and mother to the Cape.
html: 2. How she and her parents became the slaves of Mr. Zigterman? My mother suckled Mr. Zigterman's child, and I was born in his house; Mr. Zigterman brought me with my father and mother to the Cape.

text: 3.Had she ever seen either her mother's or her own certifi¬cate of freedom? No, at that period I was but a child, my mother did not show me them, and on her going to Holland she promised to return for me in two years, but in the interval she died.

text: 4. If so, when, where, with whom, and by what means?

text: 5. Does she not know that she was left by Mr. Zigterman to Mr. Blankenberg? Yes, because Mr. Blankenberg was agent to Mr. Zigterman.

text: 6. Does she not know that she was presented to Mr. Blankenberg to Johanna the wife of Mr. P. J. Truter? No, I was persuaded that my mother would in two years return to fetch me.

text: 7. Was she not given to the said daughter by Mr. Blankenberg before the marriage? I was with her before this marriage.
html: 7. Was she not given to the said daughter by Mr. Blankenberg before the marriage? I was with her before this marriage.

text: 8. What children she bore since she lived with Mr. Truter, and where they now are? None, my children Theresa, Eleonora, and Sanna were then born, I bore them when with Mr. Blankenberg.

text: The slave Clasina belonging to P. J. Truter, Esquire, having in her examination of the 21st June last declared by the Advocate Neethling appointed a trustee over the said Clasina that she had had two letters in her possession, which she had received from her mother in Holland, and which letters might serve as proofs of her freedom, though she neglected to show them to her trustee, who had repeatedly urged her to it, being now at the express desire of the Advocate Neethling required to produce the said letters, and asked whose they were, said Clasina declared that the letters were always kept preserved carefully in her chest, though they were now missing, and she believed were furtively taken away when she was extremely ill, at a time when her acquaintance had access to her chest; that according to the contents of these letters, which the old Mrs. Blankenberg had read to her, she now remembers that her father was deceased, that she must behave herself well, and that her mother at the expiration of two years would come to the Cape for her, at the same time acknowledges that not a word with regard to her freedom was contained in the above letters, but that as her mother was free she considered herself also free, especially as she was but 4 or 5 years old when she was brought hither by Governor Zigterman, who remained here but one month, and then sailed for Holland, and declares for the reasons above mentioned that she is unable to produce the letters.

text: Thursday, 2nd January, 1812.

Was heard the following report from the Member of the Court L. C. Strubberg, together and with the Secretary of the Court, in whose hands the report of the Advocate Neethling as trustee over Clasina of Bengal, with the documents relating thereto, were placed for consideration and opinion.
html: Was heard the following report from the Member of the Court L. C. Strubberg, together and with the Secretary of the Court, in whose hands the report of the Advocate Neethling as trustee over Clasina of Bengal, with the documents relating thereto, were placed for consideration and opinion.

text: Whereupon (P. J. Truter, Esquire, having withdrawn himself from deliberating on this case) it is resolved that the Committee be thanked for the trouble they had taken, and that the Court coincides with the principles laid down of the above mentioned report, and it is further declared by these presents that there is no basis for an action in support of the claim to freedom set up on the part of Clasina and her descendants, that the Advocate Neethling has discharged his duty as trustee over Clasina in this case, and is consequently released from all further, and he is hereby honorably released accordingly.

text: of Good Hope

Gentlemen,—The undersigned, to whom has been transmitted by a Resolution, dated 12th September last, taken by Commissioners from your Court, the memorial of Clasina from Bengal to His Excellency the Earl of Caledon, then Governor of this Colony, and which His Excellency was pleased to refer to you to decide upon, together with the reports of Mr. Neethling, trustee over memorialist, and the documents thereto annexed, for your guidance and advice, have thought proper after the examination of the above to attain the object which you had in view, to apply themselves to the investigation of the following points:
html: Gentlemen,—The undersigned, to whom has been transmitted by a Resolution, dated 12th September last, taken by Commissioners from your Court, the memorial of Clasina from Bengal to His Excellency the Earl of Caledon, then Governor of this Colony, and which His Excellency was pleased to refer to you to decide upon, together with the reports of Mr. Neethling, trustee over memorialist, and the documents thereto annexed, for your guidance and advice, have thought proper after the examination of the above to attain the object which you had in view, to apply themselves to the investigation of the following points:

text: 1. Upon whom in case of reclamation of freedom rests the production of proofs.
html: 1. Upon whom in case of reclamation of freedom rests the production of proofs.

text: 2. Which or what kind of proofs can be considered as sufficient.
html: 2. Which or what kind of proofs can be considered as sufficient.

text: 3. In how far she proved in this case as well with respect to herself as to her descendants.
html: 3. In how far she proved in this case as well with respect to herself as to her descendants.

text: Ad primum.— As to this point the restrictions of the Roman law, to which we are obliged to adhere until the legislature shall be pleased to alter them, are so distinct that one need only read them to know what is just on this head. It is a general, adopted principle, that the prosecutor must prove, as is also found in the Title of the Pandectem de Edendo, where it is clearly said, and applying the same to the reclamation of liberty it must of course find room here, as is stated in Lo. 7, Par. 5. From which, if made applicable to the present case, it would follow that the slave Clasina, reclaiming her own freedom and that of her descendants, ought to become the claimant and take upon herself the charge of producing proofs; whereas Mr. Truter, if Clasina had found herself bona fide free, desiring to reduce her to slavery, would be obliged according to the same law to step forward as the claimant and to prove his claim. In the same manner does the Emperor Alexander express himself in Lo. 5, viz. Probationissane, which word we cannot otherwise translate then by Trouwens...

From which, if made applicable to the present case, it would follow that the slave Clasina, reclaiming her own freedom and that of her descendants, ought to become the claimant and take upon herself the charge of producing proofs; whereas Mr. Truter, if Clasina had found herself bona fide free, desiring to reduce her to slavery, would be obliged according to the same law to step forward as the claimant and to prove his claim. In the same manner does the Emperor Alexander express himself in Lo. 5, viz. Probationissane, which word we cannot otherwise translate then by Trouwens...

text: In opposition to this it might be said that slavery is a state contrary to the laws of nature, and even according to the very same Roman laws, so that a person who takes for his basis a right which he has received from nature, could not be obliged to prove the freedom given him by nature, but though this philosophical opinion of some lawyers has had no influence on the Roman Justice, it is not the duty of a judge to employ himself in deciding abstract and philosophical opinions, but he is bound accurately to follow the strict meaning of the legislature, and to pronounce his judgment accordingly.

text: He can do this with so much the more certainty because he finds slavery as a fact existing in the infancy of mankind, adopted by all nations of the old world, extended and limited by laws, so that not only examples of it are found in the most humane laws of Moses, but even in the time of Abraham.

text: 2. As thus the reclaimer of freedom must prove his right, the undersigned will investigate into the nature of those proofs; the freedom must now be proved 1st by documents which the defendant is obliged to produce, 2ndly by witnesses who are opposed to documents which are lost and to arguments, and finally 3rdly by proper arguments and presumptions.

As thus the reclaimer of freedom must prove his right, the undersigned will investigate into the nature of those proofs; the freedom must now be proved 1st by documents which the defendant is obliged to produce, 2ndly by witnesses who are opposed to documents which are lost and to arguments, and finally 3rdly by proper arguments and presumptions.

text: 3. In how far did the memorialist prove under these circum¬stances? As to this, it is certain that the memorialist to prove her freedom did not produce witnesses, nor did she bring forward anything else to support her assertions. It is however true that as far as regards the documents memorialist has referred to two letters which she states to have received from her mother from Holland, but besides that these letters are lost according to the memorialist's own statement, the same did not contain anything relating to her freedom according to her curator Mr. J. H. Neethling's assertion, and even if they had been written according to her statement, it must have been by a person whose evidence would not be exempt from the most just suspicion.

H. Neethling's assertion, and even if they had been written according to her statement, it must have been by a person whose evidence would not be exempt from the most just suspicion.

text: As to what relates to the arguments and presumptions, though the memorialist has first stated, and afterwards retracted, in the memorial addressed to His Excellency, that her parents were free people, but if even she had not retracted, this assertion being proved, it would be decisive with regard to Kaffers, Hottentots, and other free nations, but with regard to the natives of Bengal, where slavery is known, at least has been known, in the Dutch possessions, it cannot have that force.

text: That the receiving of the holy baptism, to which the memorialist also refers, gives her no right to freedom.
html: That the receiving of the holy baptism, to which the memorialist also refers, gives her no right to freedom.

text: Firstly, because slaves of a Christian master do never obtain their freedom by baptism . . . ., and secondly because the Statutes of India dictate just the contrary, not to mention the usage in Europe with respect to fellow Christians, who though not actually slaves, are far from being free, and are kept in a servile state....

text: That though the donation of a free minor as a marriage gift is stated not to be prejudicial to liberty, the reporters could not however apply this law to the present case. Firstly because the minority of memorialist when she was given away is not proved, secondly because the proofs of liberty supposed to be maintained by law are not only at once deficient here, but also all apparent presumptions, if there are supposed to have been any, are so much weakened in consequence of the long silence of the memorialist and the credit as well of the donor as the present possessor, and to which never any doubt was attached, that it cannot be considered otherwise than as imaginary.

text: On account of what has been aforesaid, the reporters are of opinion that the request of memorialist relative to her case cannot be accorded, and having produced no proofs of her freedom, she can make no claim to the liberty as well of herself as her descendants, it having appeared to the reports that in regard to the sales made, that the respective masters and mistresses of the memorialist's descendants had power to alienate on account of their bad behaviour. The reporters however submit their opinions to the better and more enlightened judgment of the Court.

text: As some of my Parishioners who propose attending diving worship on the day of rest arrive here on the Saturday afternoon, I generally hold church for them on the evening of that day.  The following day I am occupied twice with the Christians and in the evening with the Heathens, which latter also attend the Catechism on the Wednesday evenings.

text: Sir! exclusive of the false prejudices of the so-called Christians (which in many are already overcome) there is another great obstacle in this Country to the progress of Christianity, and oh! how happy should I be could I but see this obstacle removed by our highly respected Government before my death.  It is, namely, that a Slave who is baptized may not be sold.  This circumstance is the occasion that the Proprietors of Slaves, who may perhaps possess truly Christian hearts and entertain a desire of becoming incorporated in the Church of our Lord Jesus Christ, object to their being baptized.  Much were it to be wished that the name of Slavery were not known to us! But as this is the unfortunate lot of so many of our fellow creatures in this country without the prospect of any speedy alteration therein taking place, why must these our poor fellow creatures be excluded in their humble station from the enjoyment of those religious privileges which our now glorified Mediator, by his long suffering and obedience, obtained and procured for all Description of Men?  I lay this at your Excellency's feet, and fervently pray that, if possible, a provision in this regard may be made.

heading: 1754 — Crime Records (Slaves: Raachel van de Caab)
text: 1754 — Crime Records (Slaves: Raachel van de Caab)
html: 1754 — Crime Records (Slaves: Raachel van de Caab)

text: Nademaal uijt de vrijwillige gerecolleerde confessie van Raachel van de Caab, slavin van den burger Jacobus van Reenen de Jonge, oud naar gissing 21 jaaren, thans ’s heeren gevangene, en verdere stucken ten processe gevoegt, het den E. Agbtb. Raad van Justitie des Casteels de Goede Hoop, duijdelijk is gebleeken:
html: Nademaal uijt de vrijwillige gerecolleerde confessie van Raachel van de Caab, slavin van den burger Jacobus van Reenen de Jonge, oud naar gissing 21 jaaren, thans ’s heeren gevangene, en verdere stucken ten processe gevoegt, het den E. Agbtb. Raad van Justitie des Casteels de Goede Hoop, duijdelijk is gebleeken:

text: Dat sij gevangene nu wel een week of ses geleeden door haar meede slaaf Joseph gevraagt geworden sijnde, of sij niet wist waar quick te koop was, waarmeede hij seijde knoopen en spiegels te willen schoon maaken, ende de gevangene in ’t eerst hierop geantwoord hebbende, dat sulx niet wist; heeft sij gevangene naderhand op het herhaalde versoek van hem Joseph, eerst den bij den Apothecar in ’s E. Comp. hospitaal beschijdenen slaaf diesweegens aangesprooken, dog van denselven sulx niet bekoomende, heeft de gevangene voorts, de meijd van den oud tweeden oppershirurgijn Dirck Wijdenaar, Amarentia genaamt, daarna gevraagt, van dewelke sij dan ook ’s daags voor Kersdag, een vlesje met wat quik heeft bekomen, ’tgeene sij aan voorm. Joseph overhandigt heeft; ende hij Joseph vervolgens haar gevangene tot verschijde maalen versogt hebbende, om hem te waarschouwen, wanneer haar lijfvrouw water quam te eijschen, heeft sij gevangene sulx aan hem Joseph niet alleen belooft, maar ook op den 4e deeser maand Januarij, wanneer haar lijfvrouw des avonds in de maanschijn voor de deur sat, en een glas water vroeg, voorsijde Joseph daarvan kennis gegeeven, denwelken alsdoen in het door haar gevangene schoon gemaakte en met water gevulde glas, wat quik uijt het voorseijde vlesje gegooten heeft, met bijvoeging: Geeft dat maar aan de Juffrouw, die is so valsch en sal naar de huishouding niet kunnen sien; welk glas dan ook door de gevangene dusdanig aan haar lijfvrouw overgegeeven is geworden; dog door deselve onder ’t drinken bespeurt werdende, dat er jets in het glas was, en haar gevangene daarna vroeg: repliceerde sij gevangene, niet met al, tragtende teffens het voorseijde glas water haare lijfvrouw weeder afteneemen, maar hetselve door eevengem. haare lijfvrouw naar gedaane visitatie bij de kaars, geborgen werdende, vroeg sij gevangene aan voorm. Joseph, wat dat hij gedaan hadde, en denselven haar daarop geantwoort hebbende, Nonje sal verteeren als een geraamte, is sij gevangene volgens haar voorgeeven soodanig bevreest geworden, dat sij sulx aan haar voorm. lijfvrouw ter dier tijd niet heeft derven bekent maaken, hebbende sij gevangene egter op de verdere naauwkeurige examinatie van haar lijfheer, aan haar sowel als aan voorseijde Joseph gedaan, op Maandag ofte op den 7e daaraanvolgende beleeden, dat sij niet eerder geweeten had, dat sij dan wel Joseph daarmeede jets quaat hadde gedaan, dan naar dat sij gevangene van Joseph verstaan hadde, dat haar Juffrouw daarvan verteeren soude, en is door hem Joseph tergelijkertijd met verswijging der reedenen ofte intentie die hem daartoe bewogen hadden, vrijwillig op sijn knien aan sijn lijfheer gestand gedaan, dat hij dat quick onder ’t water gegooten had, met versoek van hem sulx te willen vergeeven, op ’twelke door voorm. sijn lijfheer geantwoord is geworden: dat hij het hem wel vergeeven wilde, maar dat hij hem egter verkoopen soude; welken Joseph op Vrijdag den 11e deeser in ’t slaavenhuijs sig selfs verhangen hebbende, is de gevangene vervolgens geapprehendeert, en dus in handen der Justitie overgeleevert geworden.

text: Ende gemerkt sulk een opsettelijk quaadaardig en eenigsints bewerkstelligt voorneemen van de gevangene, aan haar lijfvrouw gepleegt, in een land daar regt en justitie geoeffent word, niet te dulden is, maar tot afschrik van andere diergelijke boosdoenders, exemplaarlijk moet worden gestraft.
html: Ende gemerkt sulk een opsettelijk quaadaardig en eenigsints bewerkstelligt voorneemen van de gevangene, aan haar lijfvrouw gepleegt, in een land daar regt en justitie geoeffent word, niet te dulden is, maar tot afschrik van andere diergelijke boosdoenders, exemplaarlijk moet worden gestraft.

text: Soo is het, dat den E. Achtb. Raad van Justitie deeses gouvernements, ten dage dienende, gesien en overwogen hebbende, den schriftelijke Crimineelen Eijsch ende Conclusie van den Heer Independent Fiscaal Pieter Reede van Oudshoorn nomine officii op ende jeegens de gevangene gedaan en genoomen, mitsgds. geleth op der gevangene eijgen libere confessie behoorlijk gerecolleert, en ’tgeene wijders ter saake dienende was, en haar E. E. Agtb. konde doen moveeren, doende regt uijt naame ende van weegens de Hoogmogende Heeren Staaten Generaal der Vereenigde Neederlanden, mitsgds. van sijne Doorlugtigste Hoogheid, den Heere Prince van Orangjen en Nassouw, als Erfstadthouder, Capitain en Admiraal Generaal van de Republicq, de gevangene Raachel van de Caab hebben gecondemneert, so als haar E. E. Agtb. deselve condemneeren mits deesen, om gebragt te worden ter plaatse alwaar men alhier gewoon is crimineele sententien uijttevoeren, en aldaar aan den scherpregter over geleevert sijnde, eerst met de strop om den hals onder de galg te pronck gestelt, vervolgens aan een paal gebonden met roeden op de bloote rugge strengelijk gegeesselt, en daarop gebrandmerkt te worden, voorts voor al haar leeven in de ketting gekloncken weesende, dus ten profijte van haaren lijfheer den burger Jacobus van Reenen de Jonge publiquelijk te worden verkogt, onder conditie dat nooijt ofte ooijt weederom in de handen van hem ofte de sijne sal moogen geraaken, met condemnatie in de costen en misen van justitie.

text: Fiat Executie, [get.] R. Tulbagh.
TRANSLATION

Since from the voluntary, verified confession of Raachel van de Caab, woman slave of the burgher Jacobus van Reenen junior, 21 years old at a guess, currently their honours’ prisoner, and from the other documents added to the case, it has evidently appeared to the honourable Council of Justice of the Castle of Good Hope:
html: Since from the voluntary, verified confession of Raachel van de Caab, woman slave of the burgher Jacobus van Reenen junior, 21 years old at a guess, currently their honours’ prisoner, and from the other documents added to the case, it has evidently appeared to the honourable Council of Justice of the Castle of Good Hope:

text: That fully six weeks ago now, the prisoner, was asked by her fellow slave Joseph if she knew where one could buy mercury with which he said he wanted to clean buttons and mirrors with, and that the prisoner at first answered to this that she did not know; however, on the persistant request of Joseph she eventually spoke about this first to the slave of the apothecary, assigned to the honourable company’s hospital, but since she did not obtain anything from him, the prisoner then asked about this the meijd, called Amarentia, of the former second chief surgeon, Dirck Wijdenaar, from whom she then indeed obtained a small bottle with some mercury on the day before Christmas and which she handed over to the aforementioned Joseph. And that Joseph then requested her on several occasions to inform him when her mistress asked for water, the prisoner not only promised this to him, but also, on the night of the 4th of this month January, when her mistress was sitting by the door in the moonlight and asked her for a glass of water, told the aforesaid Joseph of this. He then poured some mercury from the aforesaid small bottle into the glass, which had been cleaned and filled with water by the prisoner, and added: “Just give this to the juffrouw, she is so false and would not be able to look after the household”. This glass was then also handed over thus to her mistress by the prisoner, yet when she, while drinking, noticed that there was something in the glass and asked the prisoner what it was, she replied: “Nothing at all”, attempting at the same time to take from her mistress the aforesaid glass, but it was put aside by her mistress after inspecting it at the candle. The prisoner asked the aforementioned Joseph what he had done, who he answered her: “Nonje will waste away like a skeleton”, which made the prisoner, according to her assertion, so afraid that she did not dare to make this known at that time to her aforementioned mistress; however, the prisoner, during a subsequent careful interrogation by her owner – done to both her as well as to the aforesaid Joseph – confessed on the Monday, or the 7th thereupon, that she did not know that she or Joseph had done anything wicked by it until after she had understood from Joseph that her juffrouw would waste away because of it; and at the same time Joseph, while keeping silent about the reasons or intentions which had moved him to it, voluntarily confessed on his knees to his owner that he had poured the mercury into the water, requesting forgiveness, to which his owner replied that although he wanted to forgive him, he would however have to sell him. This Joseph, on Friday the 11th instant, hanged himself in the slave house; while the prisoner was afterwards apprehended and so delivered into the hands of justice.
